put_in.label: Langholm car park on Ewes Water

take_out.label: River right just below Hollows bridge

links.reason: Gauge sits at the Langholm put-in on the Esk. The guide says avoid the run if bony and that it gets harder in high water, so qualitative bounds only.
Canonbie gauge is on the same Esk, downstream near the take-out, so it reflects the same flow. Thresholds are qualitative estimates.
Ewes Water joins the run at Langholm, so this gauge helps track rises on the tributary but gives no basis for thresholds.

name: River Ettrick - Ettrickbridge to Selkirk
length_text: About 6-7 miles (3-4 miles to Colins Bridge, then 3 more to Selkirk)
time_text: 1.5 hours to Colins Bridge; about 3 hours to Selkirk

put_in.label: Lay-by before private hotel bridge above Ettrick Bridge

links.reason: Same river, downstream of the run at Lindean. Guide gives only qualitative advice: needs some water above shingle level, and spate makes it powerful and pushy.
Tima Water is an Ettrick tributary, so it tracks the run's flow. Guide gives no numbers, so thresholds are rough estimates.
Neighbouring Yarrow Water responds to similar rain, and the guide pairs the two rivers, though there are no gauge-specific figures.
Guide names Brockhoperig as the gauge mid-run; 1 m or more is ideal, 0.8 m is the minimum, and higher is better apart from road flooding.
Tima Water is a neighbouring tributary catchment close by and responds to the same rain, but the guide gives no levels for it.

put_in.label: Bridge over Glengaber Burn by farm cottage near Megget Reservoir sign

links.reason: Craig Douglas on Yarrow Water is nearby; the guide wants the Yarrow high after heavy rain, but the Megget joins below it. Thresholds are estimates.
Gordon Arms is on the Yarrow, which the Megget feeds. The guide wants the Yarrow high, but gives no numbers, so these are estimates.
Brockhoperig on neighbouring Ettrick Water responds to the same rain. It is a weak proxy with no guide numbers.

name: River Nethan - Holmhead Farm to Crossford

put_in.label: Old ford/weir below Holmhead Farm, Tillietudlem

take_out.label: A72 road bridge in Crossford

links.reason: Same river, close to the section. Guide says the gorge needs to be wet, brown and rock-covered at Crossford, so a moderately high level is likely.
Guide cites a Clyde reading at Garrion Bridge, which is near Kirkfieldbank. The reading's scale is unknown, so only a rough high-water proxy.
Clyde gauge nearest the Nethan confluence. It responds to the same rain but is a different river, so thresholds are only rough.

name: River Nith - Glen Airlie Picnic Site to Drumlanrig Bridge
section_name: Glen Airlie Picnic Site to Drumlanrig Bridge

put_in.label: Glen Airlie picnic site off the A76

take_out.label: River right at Drumlanrig Bridge on minor road to Drumlanrig Castle

links.reason: Drumlanrig gauge is on the Nith near the take-out. Run is usually paddleable, better at medium-high levels, and washes out into flat boily water when very high.
Same river upstream, so it follows the same rain response. The guide gives only qualitative levels, so thresholds are approximate.
Same river downstream, useful for trends. Thresholds are approximate because the guide is qualitative.

put_in.label: Broken weir just outside Hawick on Newcastleton road

links.reason: Same river, Slitrig gauge at Stobs Castle upstream of the run. Guide says it needs heavy rain and substantial water, so a spate level is assumed.
Teviot at Hawick sits just below the confluence and responds to the same rain, but it is a different river and the guide gives only qualitative advice.

put_in.label: Bridge on minor road to Polgown, about 3 miles along

take_out.label: A702 road bridge over the Scaur Water at Penpont

links.reason: Capenoch is on the Scar Water, which is the same river, though it sits downstream of the run. The guide says some recent rain is needed, with no figures given.
Hall Bridge on the Nith is the closest gauge on a neighbouring river. It responds to the same rain, but the guide gives only qualitative levels.

put_in.label: Old mill by road bridge on the Ross road, Sliddery

links.reason: Machrie Water is also on Arran and responds to the same rain. The guide gives no levels, so this is an assumed spate-run band.

put_in.label: Eddy upstream of Corsock Bridge, river left

take_out.label: Haugh Bridge

links.reason: Dalbeattie is on the Urr, downstream of the run. The guide's 1.3-1.5 m levels probably refer to an Urr gauge, but the gauge is not named, so the match is uncertain.
Same river (Robstone gauge, 17 km away); guide says substantial volume needed with rocks well covered, so a moderately high level is assumed.
Neighbouring Doon catchment in Ayrshire responds to similar rain; guide only gives qualitative need for good water.

name: Water of Minnoch - Stroan Bridge to Brogan Bridge

put_in.label: Stroan Bridge car park and picnic area near Loch Trool

links.reason: Same river, Minnoch Bridge is nearby. Guide says the lower run is paddleable even when low, drops after rain, and gets harder at high water.
Cree upstream gauge in the same catchment; useful for tracking rainfall response but the guide gives no numeric thresholds.

put_in.label: B7068 roadside access southwest of Langholm

take_out.label: Bridge at junction with Border Esk in Langholm

links.reason: Guide cites an Esk gauge reading about 1.5 m when the run is in condition; Langholm Bridge is the nearest Esk gauge, just downstream of the confluence.
Esk gauge further downstream at Canonbie; the guide's 1.5 m hint is ambiguous here, so a relative spate threshold is used as a trend indicator.
Neighbouring Ewes Water responds to the same rainfall, so it is useful for watching trends, but the guide gives no thresholds.
Enterkin Burn joins the Nith near Drumlanrig; the guide gives no levels, so this assumes a steep burn needs moderately high water on the nearby Nith gauge.
Scar Water is a nearby Nith-catchment tributary that responds to the same rain; it is useful for watching trends but the guide gives no thresholds.

take_out.label: Euchan Bridge, left bank well above the bridge

links.reason: Nith gauge nearest the Euchan confluence at Sanquhar; guide gives only a visual rock-cover level, so spate-type thresholds are estimated relative to typical range.
Further downstream on the Nith; useful as a trend indicator for rain in the area, with thresholds guessed from the spate character.
Nearest gauge on upper Tweed, a different river but similar hill catchment; guide says recent rain needed but not huge volumes.
Upper Tweed gauge nearby responds to the same rain; guide only gives qualitative spate guidance, so threshold is approximate.
Lugar Water is the nearest gauge, and the Glenmuir joins the Lugar. The guide only says spate is needed, so the threshold is a generic high-water estimate.
Catrine on the neighbouring Ayr catchment responds to the same rain. The guide gives only a qualitative spate requirement.

put_in.label: Above Routin Brig falls, as far up as water level suits

take_out.label: River right just below the bridge

links.reason: Cluden Water is a nearby small spate catchment and responds to the same rain; guide only asks for a medium level, so threshold is approximate.
Scar Water is a neighbouring Nith tributary with flashy response; the vague medium-level guidance gives only a rough threshold.
Neighbouring Cree tributary gauge responding to the same rain; guide gives only qualitative levels, lowish paddleable and excessive water unpaddleable.
Cree gauge at Newton Stewart is close and shows regional rain response, but the burn is a small tributary; thresholds are qualitative estimates.

put_in.label: Flat water just above the waterfall, reached by footpath carry from the hostel

links.reason: Blackwater of Dee outlet shares the name and is in the same Galloway hills, so it likely responds to similar rain. The guide gives only a qualitative high-water marker.
Small upland Galloway Dee catchment, which should react to the same rainfall. Guide thresholds are qualitative only, so the bands are estimates.
Scar Water is the nearest gauge in the Nith catchment, and Galloway rain should affect it too. It is a weak proxy with no guide numbers.

take_out.label: Bottom of the run near the loch, close to a farm

links.reason: Guide points to the Yarrow gauge; Craig Douglas is the nearer upper Yarrow gauge. Rising levels suggest runnable, spate-only stream, so moderately elevated threshold.
Gordon Arms is also on the Yarrow, which the guide recommends checking; rising readings indicate Talla should be paddleable.
Upper Tweed at Kingledores is close and responds to the same rain; spate-dependent run needs rising water.
